update description: Identify needs will require the Production and Dissemination Specialist to first scan and assess existing internal, administrative, and external data assets before proposing any new survey, collection, or special study. New collection becomes a last resort and must be justified through documented cost-benefit, timeliness, feasibility, risk, automation, reuse, and AI-readiness analysis.
impact reasoning: This update changes the role from primarily responding to client requests by defining studies and identifying data sources for bespoke outputs into a more strategic and evidence-based decision function at the front end of statistical work. The EC-05 will be expected to systematically interrogate existing data holdings and reusable assets before approving or recommending new collection activity. This will alter operational practice by adding formal discovery, assessment, documentation, and challenge functions to early-stage project definition. The role will also require more structured engagement with clients and internal partners to test whether needs can be met through reuse, linkage, existing series, administrative data, or automated solutions. Decisions will need to be digitally traceable and defensible to governance bodies, making documentation, metadata navigation, feasibility analysis, and business-case development central parts of the work. As a result, the job evolves from a special-study and production orientation toward a stronger data stewardship, data discovery, and options-analysis orientation.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - 'Develops data bases for the provision of time-series information as well as data for special studies and requests.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: This activity would shift from mainly creating or adapting databases for specific requests toward first identifying whether suitable existing datasets, linked assets, or reusable statistical products already exist. Database development would increasingly be positioned as reuse optimization, integration, or enhancement of existing assets rather than a default response to new user demand.

gaps.justification: The current wording emphasizes developing databases for requests, but the update requires a prior discovery step across existing holdings and external sources before development begins.
gaps.name: Enterprise data asset landscape knowledge
gaps.description: Knowledge of internal statistical holdings, administrative data sources, external data providers, and reusable analytical assets across the organization.

gaps.justification: To determine whether new development is needed, the role must be able to search, compare, and interpret metadata-rich assets in digital environments.
gaps.name: Metadata-assisted data discovery
gaps.description: Ability to navigate catalogues, metadata repositories, registries, and documentation systems to locate and assess fit-for-purpose data assets.

gaps.justification: The future expectation explicitly prioritizes reuse and solution-oriented thinking over creating new collection vehicles or bespoke assets.
gaps.name: Data reuse and asset rationalization
gaps.description: Ability to assess whether existing datasets, time series, linked records, or prior outputs can satisfy user needs with minimal new development.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - 'Provides subject-matter expertise and consultative services to users within and outside STC.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Consultation will become more challenging and advisory in nature. Instead of mainly helping users obtain requested outputs, the specialist will need to challenge assumptions about data needs, explain why reuse or alternative sources may be preferable, and justify when new collection is not warranted. Advice will include feasibility, burden, timeliness, automation, and governance implications.

gaps.justification: The updated role requires communicating not just data possibilities but evidence-based decisions on why a request should be met through reuse or denied as a new collection.
gaps.name: Business-case communication
gaps.description: Ability to explain and defend complex cost-benefit, timeliness, burden, and risk-based recommendations to clients and governance stakeholders.

gaps.justification: The specialist must now bring automation and AI considerations into early consultation, which is not explicit in the current role profile.
gaps.name: Automation and AI readiness concepts
gaps.description: Understanding of how automation, machine-assisted processes, and AI-enabled methods affect feasibility, efficiency, data sourcing, and option selection.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - 'Represents subject matter divisions on development projects, task forces or committees in various roles.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Representation on committees and projects would increasingly involve advocating for reuse-first approaches, documenting needs assessments, and bringing evidence on feasibility, digital integration, and data asset options into governance and decision forums.

gaps.justification: Committee participation will now require stronger governance-oriented analysis and structured justification for new or avoided collection activity.
gaps.name: Governance-oriented options analysis
gaps.description: Ability to prepare and present comparative options, including reuse, administrative data, linkage, or new collection, with documented rationale.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities - Decision making - 'Investigates client requirements for statistical information, defines the nature and scope of special studies, determines the sources of data for special requests as well as the methods and approaches to be used. Modifies existing techniques or develops new approaches to meet specific needs.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: This is the most directly affected element. The activity would be updated to require a formal sequence: identify the need, scan existing data assets, assess alternative sources, compare solution options, evaluate burden/risk/timeliness/cost, and document the rationale for any recommendation. 'Special studies' would no longer be the implicit default; instead, the role would need to prove that no suitable existing solution is available before initiating new collection or bespoke production.

gaps.justification: The update explicitly requires documented cost-benefit, timeliness, and risk assessments before new collection is initiated.
gaps.name: Cost-benefit-risk assessment
gaps.description: Ability to evaluate and document comparative costs, operational feasibility, timeliness, respondent burden, privacy, and quality risks across sourcing options.

gaps.justification: The future role requires more formal and traceable decision-making than the current text implies.
gaps.name: Decision documentation and traceability
gaps.description: Ability to produce structured records of assumptions, options considered, evidence used, and rationale for recommendations in digital workflows.

gaps.justification: The update expects the role to challenge default assumptions and validate whether a new survey is actually required.
gaps.name: Requirements challenge and needs validation
gaps.description: Ability to probe stated client demands, distinguish core need from requested method, and reformulate requirements using available data and reusable solutions.

gaps.justification: Selecting among internal, administrative, and external sources requires stronger knowledge breadth than a narrower source-identification approach.
gaps.name: Alternative data source assessment
gaps.description: Knowledge of strengths, limitations, access conditions, coverage, comparability, and risks of non-survey data sources.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities - Decision making - 'Defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources. Each project is unique in nature and decisions impact on other ongoing studies.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Project definition will become more gated and conditional. Before work plans are finalized, the specialist will need to document why the need cannot be met through existing assets and assess downstream effects on organizational resources, digital integration, and operational burden. Projects may be less 'unique' and more explicitly assessed for alignment with reusable platforms and standard approaches.

gaps.justification: The update requires evidence-based prioritization tied to reuse, automation, and resourcing implications rather than only bespoke project planning.
gaps.name: Strategic options-based project scoping
gaps.description: Ability to scope projects based on comparative sourcing options, reuse potential, and organizational capacity constraints.

gaps.justification: Formalized front-end decisions now require stronger understanding of how early choices affect downstream phases and enterprise resources.
gaps.name: End-to-end lifecycle planning knowledge
gaps.description: Knowledge of how early source-selection decisions affect design, collection, processing, dissemination, evaluation, and governance.

The specialist will need to argue for reuse, phased solutions, automation, or alternate sourcing based on documented evidence rather than only negotiating implementation details.

gaps.justification: The update explicitly emphasizes solution-oriented thinking and robust business cases for new surveys.
gaps.name: Evidence-based option negotiation
gaps.description: Ability to negotiate preferred solutions using documented comparative analysis of cost, timeliness, burden, quality, risk, and feasibility.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities - Knowledge of specialized fields - 'Knowledge of statistical theories, methods, concepts and practices used in the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data.'

gaps.justification: Current knowledge focuses on handling statistical data once in use, but the update requires earlier-stage discovery and suitability assessment.

gaps.justification: The future expectation explicitly requires proactive scanning of all existing data holdings and alternative data sources first.
gaps.name: Enterprise and external data ecosystem knowledge
gaps.description: Knowledge of organizational data inventories, administrative sources, external providers, access pathways, stewardship responsibilities, and source constraints.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities - Contextual knowledge - 'Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, data quality), practices and classification systems to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of statistical projects and activities.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: This element will need to be applied earlier in the process during source selection and business-case development, not only during project conduct. gaps.justification: The update requires early risk assessment before initiating collection or selecting alternatives, extending policy application into front-end decision-making.

gaps.justification: The current role mentions integrating sources, but the update requires assessing them earlier and more systematically as alternatives to new collection.

gaps.description: Ability to compare data sources for conceptual fit, coverage, timeliness, quality, integration potential, and operational viability before initiating work.

gaps.justification: The future state explicitly mentions feasibility, automation, and AI considerations during early stakeholder engagement and solution selection.
gaps.name: Digital workflow, automation, and AI applicability

affected work-description elements.element: Job Poster - Experience - 'Providing consultative services to internal or external users.'

gaps.justification: Future consultation is more governance-heavy and analytically structured than the generic consultative expectation currently stated.
gaps.name: Structured advisory and recommendation development
gaps.description: Ability to convert user needs into documented options, recommendations, and defensible business cases.

affected work-description elements.element: Job Poster - Experience - 'Planning and organizing statistical projects, work plans, production schedules, and dissemination activities.'

gaps.justification: The update changes planning from implementation-focused scheduling to earlier options appraisal and go/no-go justification.

gaps.description: Ability to conduct front-end planning that includes source discovery, feasibility review, and decision gates before formal project launch.

gaps.name: Data discovery and source evaluation
gaps.description: Ability to identify candidate data assets, evaluate fitness for purpose, and select among them before extraction or transformation work starts.

affected work-description elements.element: Job Poster - Skills - 'Database management'

gaps.justification: The future workflow is driven by discovery and reuse across holdings, not only management of known databases.
gaps.name: Enterprise data environment navigation
gaps.description: Ability to work across repositories, metadata systems, and catalogues to identify, access, and compare relevant data assets.

affected work-description elements.element: Job Poster - Domain Knowledge - 'Survey collection processes'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Survey process knowledge remains important, but it will need to be reframed as one option among several rather than the implicit baseline solution. The role must understand when survey collection is unnecessary or unjustified relative to administrative or existing data reuse.

gaps.justification: The update explicitly establishes new data collection as a last resort, creating a gap if the role is primarily grounded in survey-centric thinking.
gaps.name: Non-survey sourcing strategy
gaps.description: Knowledge of how administrative, existing program, external, and linked data can substitute for or complement surveys.

update description: Consulting and confirming user needs will shift from initiating new collection or special studies toward first assessing existing and alternative data holdings through AI-supported discovery platforms, shared metadata, and automated feasibility tools. Consultations will become faster, more iterative, outcome-driven, and will require explicit documentation of trade-offs, reusability, value, and cost-benefit before any new survey or custom study is justified.
impact reasoning: This update changes the EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist's front-end consultative function from a primarily expert-driven, bespoke requirements definition process into a digitally enabled, evidence-based triage and assessment function. The role will no longer assume that client needs are best addressed through special studies or new collection activity. Instead, the specialist will be expected to rapidly identify what can be satisfied through existing statistical assets, linked holdings, historical series, administrative data, and reusable products, while explaining feasibility, limitations, quality implications, timeliness, and organizational prioritization criteria. This increases the importance of metadata literacy, platform-enabled consultation, and structured documentation of why certain options are recommended or rejected. Operationally, the role becomes more agile and iterative, with more frequent stakeholder interactions supported by digital tools and decision-support outputs. Responsibilities also expand to include transparent explanation of trade-offs and stronger alignment of consultation outcomes with strategic reuse, efficiency, and value-for-money objectives. The future role evolves from defining studies and sourcing data on a case-by-case basis toward facilitating informed decisions using organizational data holdings and automated discovery capabilities.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - 'Provides subject-matter expertise and consultative services to users within and outside STC.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: This activity will shift from broad consultative support oriented toward responding to requests and defining custom outputs to a more structured facilitation role using digital discovery environments. Consultative services will increasingly involve guiding users through available holdings, metadata, quality indicators, reuse options, and trade-offs rather than primarily eliciting requirements for new studies. The specialist will need to support real-time, evidence-based discussions using platform outputs and organizational prioritization criteria.

gaps.justification: Current wording emphasizes subject-matter expertise and consultation, but does not explicitly require digital discovery platform use, AI-supported consultation, or metadata-guided facilitation. The future consultation model depends on these capabilities.
gaps.name: Digital data discovery and consultation platform proficiency
gaps.description: Ability to use enterprise data discovery platforms, metadata catalogues, search interfaces, and AI-assisted consultation tools to identify reusable data assets and support rapid client discussions.

gaps.justification: The updated role requires the specialist to explain quality, timeliness, feasibility, and value trade-offs transparently during consultations, which is more explicit and structured than in the current description.
gaps.name: Trade-off facilitation and decision explanation
gaps.description: Ability to lead structured discussions on fitness-for-use, quality, timeliness, cost, and reusability, and explain why some options are preferred or rejected.

gaps.justification: The current work-description references knowledge of users and provision of advice, but not deep operational knowledge of discoverable enterprise holdings required to support first-use of existing assets.
gaps.name: Enterprise data holdings and metadata knowledge
gaps.description: Knowledge of available internal datasets, linked assets, administrative sources, historical series, metadata standards, and their reuse constraints to support needs assessment without defaulting to new collection.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - 'Develops data bases for the provision of time-series information as well as data for special studies and requests.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: This activity will be reframed away from frequent development of bespoke databases for special requests toward maximizing reuse of existing data assets, discoverable holdings, and reusable data products. New database or data product development will more often follow an explicit assessment showing that current assets cannot meet the need. The role therefore becomes more selective and justification-oriented in initiating custom outputs.

gaps.justification: The current activity assumes ongoing development for special studies and requests. The future state requires a stronger capability to assess reuse potential before building new products.
gaps.name: Data asset reuse assessment
gaps.description: Ability to evaluate whether existing datasets, time series, linked holdings, or standard products can satisfy user requirements before developing new data structures or bespoke outputs.

gaps.justification: The specialist will need to justify when new products are not warranted and when alternatives better align with organizational priorities.
gaps.name: Organizational prioritization and cost-benefit criteria
gaps.description: Knowledge of strategic prioritization frameworks, value-for-money principles, and business rules used to determine whether custom development or new collection is justified.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities - Decision making - 'Investigates client requirements for statistical information, defines the nature and scope of special studies, determines the sources of data for special requests as well as the methods and approaches to be used. Modifies existing techniques or develops new approaches to meet specific needs.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: This decision-making function is directly transformed. Investigation of requirements will now begin with a structured exploration of existing data holdings and alternative sources using automated discovery and metadata tools. Defining special studies will become a later-stage option rather than an initial response. The specialist will need to determine not only sources and methods, but also whether new work is warranted at all after documented feasibility and cost-benefit review. Decision-making will therefore become more comparative, transparent, and constrained by reuse-first principles.

gaps.justification: Current decision-making expects the specialist to define special studies and determine data sources, but not to conduct formal reuse-first digital triage supported by automated tools.
gaps.name: AI-augmented feasibility assessment
gaps.description: Ability to use AI-supported discovery and decision-support tools to assess whether existing data assets can meet stated needs, including feasibility, timeliness, and quality implications.

gaps.justification: The future expectation includes documented justification for launching new surveys or custom studies, which is not explicit in the current description.
gaps.name: Structured options analysis and justification writing
gaps.description: Ability to document decision pathways, compare options, record rationale for rejecting or approving new collection, and produce clear audit-ready justification.

gaps.justification: The updated process requires explicit evaluation of value, reuse, and organizational trade-offs in addition to technical method selection.
gaps.name: Fitness-for-use and value assessment principles
gaps.description: Knowledge of how to assess data suitability against intended use, including quality dimensions, comparability, timeliness, burden, and expected value.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities - Communication - 'Provides expert advice and guidance to all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics, on statistical program results, methods, concepts and techniques applied and on trends and developments in economic, sociological or related data programs.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: The advisory role will increasingly require immediate, consultation-stage interpretation of what existing holdings can deliver and what trade-offs are involved, rather than primarily explaining completed outputs or established methods. Advice will become more interactive, platform-enabled, and tied to data availability, metadata evidence, and transparent constraints. The specialist will need to communicate limitations and alternatives in a highly practical and time-sensitive way.

gaps.justification: Current communication expectations focus on explaining methods and results, but the future role requires live guidance based on digital discovery outputs and reusable data options.
gaps.name: Real-time evidence-based client communication
gaps.description: Ability to interpret and communicate discovery results, metadata, feasibility indicators, and trade-offs clearly during rapid iterative stakeholder discussions.

gaps.justification: The future consultation model increases the need to explain not only what is possible, but why some requests should not proceed.
gaps.name: Constraint and rationale communication
gaps.description: Ability to communicate limitations, prioritization logic, and rejection rationales constructively while maintaining stakeholder trust and engagement.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities - Communication - 'Presents arguments and options and negotiates resources, timeframes and costs with service providers (e.g. system specialists, regional office staff, survey methodologists, contractors, etc.) and clients within and outside the department.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Negotiation will become more explicitly grounded in organizational prioritization, reuse-first options, and evidence from automated feasibility tools. Rather than negotiating mainly how to execute a requested study, the specialist will more often negotiate whether a request should proceed as scoped, be satisfied through existing products, be modified, or be declined. This adds stronger challenge function and prioritization-based negotiation responsibilities.

gaps.justification: The current role includes negotiation of resources, timeframes, and costs, but the future state requires stronger negotiation around reuse, prioritization, and option constraints informed by platform evidence.
gaps.name: Prioritization-based negotiation
gaps.description: Ability to negotiate with clients using evidence on existing asset availability, organizational priorities, cost-benefit, and operational constraints rather than assuming bespoke delivery.

gaps.justification: The negotiation basis shifts toward enterprise strategy and transparent value assessment, which requires broader contextual understanding than currently stated.
gaps.name: Strategic service prioritization knowledge
gaps.description: Knowledge of how organizational priorities, service standards, burden considerations, and efficiency objectives shape acceptance, modification, or rejection of client requests.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities - Contextual knowledge - 'Knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for complex statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide advice on program results.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Knowledge of users will remain important but will be broadened to include understanding how to map user needs onto existing data ecosystems and service models rather than identifying demand for new studies alone. The notion of 'new markets' will increasingly depend on discoverability and reusability of existing assets. The specialist will need to understand user needs in terms of fit to available holdings, not just desired outputs.

gaps.justification: Current knowledge focuses on user needs and markets, but the future state requires stronger capability to connect these needs to what is already available across the agency.
gaps.name: User-needs-to-data-holdings mapping knowledge
gaps.description: Knowledge of how common stakeholder needs align with existing products, reusable assets, metadata structures, and service pathways.

gaps.justification: The update emphasizes digital consultation and rapid iterative interactions, which implies a more service-design-oriented understanding of users than currently stated.
gaps.name: Digital client journey facilitation
gaps.description: Ability to guide clients through structured digital consultation workflows that surface options, constraints, and next steps efficiently.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities - Contextual knowledge - 'Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination to user and/or subject matter clients.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: This knowledge area will expand beyond dissemination formatting and policy into awareness of discoverability, metadata exposure, reusable product access, and how holdings are presented in consultation platforms. gaps.justification: Current contextual knowledge addresses dissemination policies, but not the discoverability and metadata presentation layer central to future consultations.
gaps.name: Data discoverability and metadata presentation knowledge
gaps.description: Knowledge of how datasets, products, and metadata are catalogued, exposed, and interpreted within organizational discovery and dissemination environments.

gaps.description: Knowledge of metadata structures, interoperability principles, and system features that enable assets from different programs to be discovered and compared consistently.

gaps.justification: As consultation becomes dependent on automated tools, the specialist must understand how those tools support or constrain feasibility analysis.

gaps.description: Ability to assess the usefulness, limitations, and output quality of automated discovery and consultation tools in supporting user-needs assessment.

gaps.justification: Existing skill wording does not fully cover metadata-driven discovery or AI-supported search across enterprise holdings.

gaps.description: Ability to search, interpret, and assess datasets and related metadata across enterprise repositories to support reuse-first consultation.

affected work-description elements.element: Job Poster - Skills - 'Data manipulation'

affected work-description elements.element: Job Poster - Domain Knowledge - 'Data dissemination'

gaps.justification: Current domain knowledge does not explicitly include the emerging front-end discovery and reuse layer of service delivery.
gaps.name: Discovery-to-dissemination service model knowledge
gaps.description: Knowledge of how user needs move from discovery of available assets through feasibility assessment to dissemination of reusable or adapted outputs.

update description: Establishing output objectives must default to reuse of existing data holdings and require evidence that alternative or administrative data cannot meet needs before any new survey activity is proposed. Objectives must also embed automation, machine-readability, interoperability, and digital execution constraints from the outset, with stronger resource discipline and explicit justification for any manual or custom methods.
impact reasoning: This update changes the EC-05 Production and Dissemination Specialist's role at the objective-setting stage from primarily defining scope, sources, and approaches based on client needs and subject-matter fit to a more constrained and evidence-based function. The role will need to establish project objectives through a digital-first decision framework that prioritizes reuse of existing statistical and administrative holdings, assesses interoperability and machine-readability requirements before work begins, and documents why non-reuse or manual approaches are necessary. This shifts the work-description toward earlier and more formal engagement with data architecture, operational feasibility, automation design, and governance requirements. The Specialist will also need to justify resource use more rigorously and collaborate more directly with IT, metadata, and data-governance functions when defining studies, special requests, dissemination outputs, or processing approaches.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - "Develops data bases for the provision of time-series information as well as data for special studies and requests."
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: This activity would shift from primarily building or adapting data bases for user needs toward first assessing whether existing internal or administrative data assets can be reused, linked, or repurposed. New database development would more often require proof that reuse is insufficient, and outputs would need to be designed to support machine-readable, interoperable, and automation-ready production and dissemination.

gaps.justification: The current work-description emphasizes database development and special-study support, but does not explicitly require default reuse assessment, interoperability-by-design, or digital output constraints.
gaps.name: Internal data asset and enterprise data architecture knowledge
gaps.description: Knowledge of existing internal data holdings, administrative data options, metadata structures, enterprise data architecture, and how these can be reused or linked before creating new collection or storage solutions.

gaps.justification: The future state requires outputs to be automation-enabled, machine-readable, and interoperable from the outset, which is not explicit in the current description.
gaps.name: Digital-first output and data design
gaps.description: Ability to design databases and outputs that support structured, machine-readable, interoperable, and reusable statistical production and dissemination.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - "Provides subject-matter expertise and consultative services to users within and outside STC."
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Consultative services would increasingly include advising users that requests must align with reuse-first, automation-ready, and interoperable delivery models. The role would need to guide users away from bespoke solutions unless a documented business case supports them.

gaps.justification: The consultative role currently focuses on subject-matter expertise and user service, but the update requires stronger challenge, justification, and digital feasibility framing in consultations.
gaps.name: Digital feasibility advisory skill
gaps.description: Ability to assess and explain whether requested outputs can be delivered through reusable, automated, and interoperable methods rather than bespoke or manual approaches.

gaps.justification: The role must now explain agency-wide automation and interoperability criteria as part of requirement definition.
gaps.name: Automation and interoperability standards knowledge
gaps.description: Knowledge of organizational standards for automation, machine-readability, interoperability, and digital execution constraints relevant to statistical outputs.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities - "Represents subject matter divisions on development projects, task forces or committees in various roles."
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Representation on projects and committees would increasingly require the Specialist to advocate for reuse-first approaches, digital constraints, and enterprise alignment in cross-functional discussions, including early coordination with IT and governance stakeholders.

gaps.justification: The update introduces stronger front-end collaboration with IT and governance experts than is presently stated.
gaps.name: Cross-functional digital governance collaboration
gaps.description: Ability to work effectively with IT, metadata, architecture, and governance specialists to align objectives, data sourcing, and delivery design.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities - 1. Decision making - "Investigates client requirements for statistical information, defines the nature and scope of special studies, determines the sources of data for special requests as well as the methods and approaches to be used. Modifies existing techniques or develops new approaches to meet specific needs."
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: This is the most directly affected decision-making element. It would be updated so that determining sources and methods begins with a structured assessment of existing internal and administrative data, automation potential, interoperability, and digital feasibility. Developing new approaches would require explicit documentation of why standard reusable approaches are insufficient.

gaps.justification: The future expectation requires a formal reuse-first and justification-based sourcing framework not currently reflected in the role.
gaps.name: Reuse-first data source assessment
gaps.description: Ability to systematically evaluate existing data holdings, administrative data, and alternative sources before recommending new survey or bespoke approaches.

gaps.justification: The role now must demonstrate infeasibility of alternatives and assess digital execution constraints, which goes beyond current subject-matter and client-needs analysis.
gaps.name: Digital and operational feasibility assessment
gaps.description: Ability to assess technical, operational, automation, and interoperability feasibility of proposed outputs and methods at project initiation.

gaps.justification: The update requires stronger evidence and structured rationale for choosing methods and data sources.
gaps.name: Justification and decision documentation
gaps.description: Ability to document evidence, trade-offs, and rationale for source selection, manual exceptions, and methodological choices in a standardized way.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities - 1. Decision making - "Defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources. Each project is unique in nature and decisions impact on other ongoing studies."
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Project objectives and work plans would need to include digital execution requirements, automation assumptions, interoperability constraints, and resource discipline at initiation. The notion that each project is unique would be moderated by stronger use of standard reusable approaches and enterprise design rules.

gaps.justification: The current planning emphasis does not explicitly require digital-first constraints or standardization of objective-setting.
gaps.name: Digital project scoping frameworks
gaps.description: Knowledge of how to incorporate automation, interoperability, machine-readability, and reuse requirements into project objectives, priorities, and work plans.

gaps.justification: The future state requires trade-off assessment across reuse, manual effort, and scalability.
gaps.name: Cost-benefit and trade-off analysis for digital scoping
gaps.description: Ability to evaluate resource implications and trade-offs among reuse, new collection, automation, customization, and long-term scalability.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities - 1. Decision making - "Develops guidelines for the design, evaluation and testing of processing systems and applications and recommends modifications and improvements to existing procedures."
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Guidelines for design and evaluation would need to incorporate automation-by-default, interoperability, and machine-readable outputs as baseline requirements, rather than optional design considerations.

gaps.justification: Current guideline development is broad, but the future state requires explicit incorporation of digital standards into design and evaluation criteria.
gaps.name: Processing design standards for interoperability and automation
gaps.description: Knowledge of how to translate automation, interoperability, and digital execution requirements into system and process design guidance.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities - 3. Communication - "Provides expert advice and guidance to all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics, on statistical program results, methods, concepts and techniques applied and on trends and developments in economic, sociological or related data programs."
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Advice would increasingly need to include explanations of why reuse-first approaches, administrative data options, and digital delivery constraints shape what can be produced, how quickly, and at what cost.

gaps.justification: The role must communicate not only statistical concepts but also digital delivery and sourcing constraints to varied stakeholders.
gaps.name: Communication of digital sourcing and delivery constraints
gaps.description: Ability to explain reuse-first logic, automation requirements, interoperability constraints, and the rationale for rejecting bespoke or manual options.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities - 3. Communication - "Presents arguments and options and negotiates resources, timeframes and costs with service providers (e.g. system specialists, regional office staff, survey methodologists, contractors, etc.) and clients within and outside the department."
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Negotiation would become more evidence-based and constrained by digital-first requirements. The Specialist would need to negotiate within predefined expectations for reuse, standardization, and automation rather than mainly balancing service flexibility, time, and cost.

gaps.justification: The update changes the basis of negotiation from flexible service design to digitally constrained objective-setting and sourcing choices.
gaps.name: Evidence-based negotiation in digital operating environments
gaps.description: Ability to negotiate scope, timelines, and methods using documented feasibility, reuse assessments, and automation/interoperability requirements.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities - 4. Knowledge of specialized fields - "Knowledge of statistical theories, methods, concepts and practices used in the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data."
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: This knowledge area would expand beyond statistical manipulation and retrieval to include enterprise data reuse, digital data structures, interoperability requirements, and automation-enabled data flows.

gaps.justification: The future role depends on broader digital and architectural knowledge than traditional statistical data handling alone.
gaps.name: Interoperable and automation-enabled data management knowledge
gaps.description: Knowledge of data structures, metadata, interfaces, standards, and workflow design that support automated, reusable, and interoperable statistical production.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities - 5. Contextual knowledge - "Knowledge of the mandate, objectives and organization of Statistics Canada to manage subject matter studies, surveys and projects. Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend changes to other statistical programs."
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: This element would be updated to place stronger emphasis on enterprise-wide awareness of internal data assets, cross-program reuse opportunities, and organizational digital architecture to support objective-setting and source selection.

gaps.justification: The current wording includes knowledge of other programs, but the future expectation requires more systematic enterprise-wide asset awareness and reuse capability.
gaps.name: Enterprise-wide data holdings and reuse landscape knowledge
gaps.description: Knowledge of available internal program data, administrative sources, metadata inventories, and reuse pathways across the organization.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities - 6. Research and analysis - "Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, classification, coding systems and report formats or develops new ones to meet specific needs."
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Approval of parameters, coding systems, and report formats would be more tightly tied to machine-readability, interoperability, and standardization, reducing tolerance for custom formats unless justified.

gaps.justification: The future state requires parameter and format decisions to support digital interoperability and standardization by default.
gaps.name: Standards-based format and parameter design
gaps.description: Ability to define or approve classifications, coding structures, and report formats that support interoperability, machine-readability, and automated downstream use.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities - 6. Research and analysis - "Evaluates the impact of technological developments on respondent operation and production procedures and prepares reports recommending appropriate approaches and guidelines."
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: This element would expand from reacting to technological developments to proactively assessing whether emerging technologies improve reuse, reduce manual effort, and enable scalable digital output design during objective setting.

gaps.justification: The role must now evaluate technology at the front end of project scoping, not only as a later operational consideration.
gaps.name: Technology assessment for digital statistical production
gaps.description: Ability to assess how tools, platforms, and automation capabilities affect source selection, production design, and dissemination feasibility.

affected work-description elements.element: Technical Activities - 6. Research and analysis - "Research and analysis are required to evaluate the effectiveness of processing systems, to formulate computer systems specifications, to design and create test procedures and acceptance criteria to ensure that processing systems yield the desired outputs."
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Research and analysis would increasingly be required earlier in the lifecycle to define digital acceptance criteria tied to automation, reuse, interoperability, and scalable execution before objectives are approved.

gaps.justification: The future role requires objective-stage digital acceptance logic, which is more upstream than the current processing-system focus.
gaps.name: Digital acceptance criteria and scalable execution knowledge
gaps.description: Knowledge of how to define criteria for automation readiness, interoperability compliance, and scalable digital execution during planning and objective approval.

affected work-description elements.element: Job Poster - Skills - "Data manipulation"
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Data manipulation remains relevant but would need to evolve from operational handling of data toward evaluating reusable sources and designing data flows suited to automation and interoperability.

gaps.justification: Current skill wording is operationally focused and does not capture reuse-first or automation-oriented application.
gaps.name: Reusable data flow design
gaps.description: Ability to structure and transform data in ways that support reuse, standardized ingestion, and automated production pipelines.

affected work-description elements.element: Job Poster - Skills - "Database management"
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Database management would increasingly require understanding enterprise metadata, interoperable schemas, and shared data asset use rather than only maintaining program-specific stores.

gaps.justification: The future work-description requires database-related decisions to align with enterprise architecture and reuse principles.
gaps.name: Enterprise metadata and interoperable schema knowledge
gaps.description: Knowledge of metadata management, common structures, and schema design principles that support data reuse and interoperability.

affected work-description elements.element: Job Poster - Skills - "Project planning"
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Project planning would need to include explicit feasibility evidence, digital constraints, automation assumptions, and justification for deviations from standard reusable approaches.

gaps.justification: Current planning expectations do not explicitly include digital-first gating and justification requirements.
gaps.name: Digital-first planning and gating
gaps.description: Ability to build plans that incorporate reuse assessments, automation requirements, interoperability constraints, and exception-based approval logic.

affected work-description elements.element: Job Poster - Domain Knowledge - "Statistical infrastructure"
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: This domain knowledge would need to broaden from understanding infrastructure components to understanding how enterprise statistical infrastructure supports reuse-first sourcing, automation, interoperability, and digital execution at initiation.

gaps.justification: The future role relies on stronger architectural understanding than the current domain label implies.
gaps.name: Digital statistical architecture knowledge
gaps.description: Knowledge of how statistical infrastructure, platforms, metadata services, and governance frameworks support automated and interoperable production.

affected work-description elements.element: Job Poster - Domain Knowledge - "Data dissemination"
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Data dissemination would increasingly be planned from the outset as structured, machine-readable, and interoperable output delivery rather than mainly as an end-stage publication consideration.

gaps.justification: The update embeds output design constraints at objective-setting, creating a stronger linkage between planning and dissemination architecture.
gaps.name: Machine-readable dissemination design knowledge
gaps.description: Knowledge of dissemination formats, standards, and delivery models that enable structured, machine-readable, and interoperable outputs.
